competitors.rationale: Verified on 2026-08-12 (C:FridgeChef). Solves the inventory input problem through photo recognition to suggest recipes, but targets solo improvisers rather than households, and lacks weekly dinner planning, shopping lists, and shared coordination.

competitors.pricing_summary: EUR 6.99/month or EUR 49.99/year (converted: approx. EUR 4.17/month on annual plan)
competitors.rationale: Verified on 2026-07-30 (C:MealLoop). Directly serves families with weekly meal plans, automated grocery lists, and family sharing. However, it does not track existing household inventory.

Verified on 2024-11-05 (C:PlanPlate), making the data nearly two years old and possibly outdated. Offers calendar planning and sharing for couples and flatmates, but lacks inventory tracking and automated list generation.

Verified on 2026-06-18 (C:PantryGenie). Excellent inventory tracking via barcode scanning, expiry alerts, and shopping lists aimed at waste reduction, but does not generate weekly dinner plans or coordinate household meal decisions.

competitors.pricing_summary: Free; EUR 29.99 one-off for full recipe pack
competitors.rationale: Verified on 2026-05-02, but lacks a source URL in research records (C:WeekWise). Focuses on budget filters and price comparison meal plans, but does not connect to existing fridge or pantry inventory.

Verified on 2025-01-20 via home page rather than pricing page, making it potentially outdated (C:ZeroWaste Kitchen). Focuses on ad-hoc leftover recipe ideas, lacking structured weekly planning, inventory management, or shopping list automation.

Verified on 2026-08-25 (C:SupperSync). Strong competitor for household dinner planning with shared schedules, cooking rotas, and shared shopping lists, but does not account for existing inventory in fridges or pantries.

white_space: No single competitor integrates inventory awareness with automated weekly meal planning and shopping lists. Competitors either track inventory and leftover recipes without weekly planning (C:FridgeChef, C:PantryGenie, C:ZeroWaste Kitchen) or provide weekly plans and shared lists without knowing what the household already owns (C:MealLoop, C:PlanPlate, C:SupperSync, C:WeekWise).
No competitor combines household coordination and chore assignment (who cooks) with dynamic inventory-based meal generation (C:SupperSync, C:PantryGenie).
pricing_anchors: Competitor monthly subscription list prices range from EUR 2.99/month (C:PlanPlate) to EUR 6.99/month (C:MealLoop; EUR 49.99/year converts to EUR 4.17/month), with middle anchors at EUR 3.99/month (C:PantryGenie), EUR 4.49/month per household (C:SupperSync), and EUR 4.99/month (C:FridgeChef). Consumer stated median willingness to pay is EUR 3.50 per month (S05). The viable pricing band is EUR 2.99 to EUR 6.99 per month; any price above EUR 6.99 per month is unsupported and untested.

idea_claim_checks.claim: a lot of food gets thrown away
idea_claim_checks.explanation: Supported by S01, which documents that households discard roughly a fifth (19%) of the food they buy.

idea_claim_checks.claim: Existing recipe apps give ideas but do not know what you already own.
idea_claim_checks.explanation: Contradicted by competitor data. FridgeChef suggests recipes directly from photos of your fridge (C:FridgeChef), and PantryGenie tracks pantry inventory with barcode scanning and expiry alerts (C:PantryGenie). The true gap is not knowing inventory alone, but combining inventory awareness with weekly dinner planning and household coordination.
